assertion: The September 2026 FSSAI register lists Biokraft Foods Private Limited’s Cultivated Chicken-based Product at row 28, file 80/Std/PA/FSSAI/2025, receipt 20 August 2025, stage 7. Its legend combines clarification, approval and rejection; the displayed code does not establish which decision occurred.
limits: A named administrative record is now located; actual decision, approved process and certification remain unestablished.

assertion: Notification 34/2024-25 adds conditions for specified products exported as halal-certified to listed destinations, including i-CAS facilities, NABCB-accredited certification and applicable importing-country requirements. Non-halal-certified export procedures are left unchanged. Paragraph 2 restricts the additions to listed tariff codes.
limits: No 0207 poultry code is listed in this instrument, but the classification of a cultivated product is not supplied; neither blanket inclusion nor exemption follows. No domestic food approval follows.

assertion: Notification 59/2025-26 adds twenty destinations to 34/2024-25. The additional countries other than Egypt receive a two-week transition from 9 February 2026. Notification 28/2026-27 replaces Egypt’s original six-month period with nine months from 9 February 2026, leaving other provisions unchanged.
limits: This describes the retrieved amendment chain, not every later export rule. The time origin is February, not August.

assertion: The 2025 constitutional edition retains sect-specific interpretation for Muslim personal law in Article 227 and representation of different schools on the Council of Islamic Ideology where practicable in Article 228. These provisions establish neither population proportions nor one national madhhab.
limits: Legal and institutional scope only.

assertion: Article 229 in the 2025 edition uses a one-fourth legislative referral threshold; its footnote attributes replacement of two-fifths to the 2024 amendment. Article 230 gives advice/recommendation functions and its revised paragraph 4 requires consideration of the final report within twelve months after laying.
limits: The 2017 hosted edition is not a substitute for this version. Its Article 230(2) prints 299, while the 2025 version prints 229; preserve the discrepancy rather than silently correcting a quotation.

assertion: Punjab Food Authority guidance describes registration for products sold in Punjab, including goods produced elsewhere, and lists ingredient information, analyses, raw-material halal certificates, labeling and shelf-life documents. Scrutiny, sampling and competent-authority approval precede issuance of a registration certificate.
limits: General provincial procedure; no cultivated-chicken authorization, accepted manufacturing dossier or nationwide scope established.

assertion: Act 505’s 2013 reprint directs the Federal Territories Mufti ordinarily to accepted Shafii views, permits named other schools where that conflicts with public interest, and ultimately permits the Mufti’s judgment under the specified conditions. Section 34 makes gazetting a prerequisite to the stated fatwa status and territorial legal effect.
limits: Not a national demographic claim, not every state’s law, and not proof of current consolidated wording or a particular national-committee opinion’s legal effect.

assertion: The saved FSSAI page component labels a link as the 2017 approval regulation, but the retrieved 43-page PDF is an application-status register dated 4 January 2023. It was rejected as evidence of the regulation text.
locator: Page-component Regulation block and downloaded PDFpage 1/footer
limits: A source-identity finding for the saved response; no claim about whether the endpoint will return the same bytes later.

assertion: The inspected Article 12 names Islam and the Twelver Jafari school while recognizing specified other schools for rites, education, personal status and qualified local rules.
limits: Describes the retrieved constitutional wording. It does not measure prevalence, establish implementation, or verify a complete current consolidation.

assertion: The 2025 amendment provides conditional Jafari personal-status choices and assigns a drafting/advisory role to the Shia Endowment Scientific Council. Decision 10 subsequently approves the code as an annex, effective on gazette publication.
locator: Law Article 1; Decision first/second clauses; Gazette 4843 dated 6 October 2025
limits: Personal status is not an exclusive national madhhab, a food-approval framework or a demographic statistic. Underlying Arabic and the full code need qualified legal review.

assertion: Articles 2–3 in WIPO’s 2015 compilation name Islam and Islamic Sharia without naming a juristic school in those provisions. The compilation appends a 2015 transitional declaration.
limits: This is a bounded reading of these provisions, not proof that no other law names a school or that this is an uncontested current governing instrument.

assertion: Pew’s 2009 estimate gives Shia affiliation as 90–95% of Iran’s Muslim population.
limits: Historical broad affiliation estimate, not a measured 2026 or Jafari-school share.

assertion: Pew’s 2009 estimate gives 65–70% Shia among Iraq’s Muslims. A later summary reports a late-2011 survey with 51% Shia, 42% Sunni and 5% just a Muslim.
locator: 2009 Iraq table row; 2014 article on late-2011 survey
limits: Keep estimates and survey self-identification separate. Neither result is a current census, and their difference is not a time-series change estimate; do not allocate the unreported remainder.

assertion: Pew’s 2009 estimate gives Shia affiliation as 35–40% of Yemen’s Muslim population.
limits: Historical broad affiliation estimate, not a measured Zaydi, regional northern-Yemen or current population share.

assertion: The official-hosted English constitutional text, Article 2, identifies Islam as state religion and Sharia as a main legislative source; that clause names no juristic school.
limits: Consolidation and later constitutional measures not checked. Not a claim that no other Kuwaiti law names a school.

assertion: The official-hosted constitutional explanatory memorandum discusses Sharia as a legislative source when explaining Article 1.
limits: Current operative Article1 and2024 amendments not established by this extract. Does not establish Hanbali population predominance or an official national school.

limits: Historical estimate only;2026 value unknown. Not citizens-only, not percentage of all residents, not measured madhhab adherence; no Sunni or Ibadi remainder computed.

limits: Named-author transcription only. His assertion of agreement is not independently demonstrated consensus. No authenticated print edition, qualified translation, separated-serum ruling or cultivated-cell analogy is established.
